intro: Three things called 'world', three sizes, three names — frozen because the confusion was made once.

rings.label: WORLD VERSION · a manifest root · KB
WRL GRAPH · the semantic layer · KB – MB

steps.caption: WORLD is the persistent, machine-sized environment: the user's machine, 10 GB to 10 TB. It is what is backed up.
WORLD VERSION is a content-addressed description of that machine at one instant. Kilobytes. It is a root, not the world.
steps.takeaway: A version is a root that names a state; it is not the state.

steps.caption: WRL GRAPH is the semantic, topological and control layer inside a world — with its own head.
The error, once: a 247 KB WRL layer was reported as a conclusion about a 10 TB product. 0.21 % was mistaken for the whole.
steps.takeaway: There is no current_head field anywhere: a head is always qualified — manifest_root or wrl_head.

steps.caption: Frozen vocabulary in CLOUD_V1.md §2. Conflating them is the recorded failure this pattern exists to prevent.
steps.takeaway: When one word means three sizes, give each size its own word and refuse the bare one.
